_comment: Shared truth table for session.label.json READING (docs/session-identity.md, G-series). `input` is the EXACT bytes of the file, or null meaning 'no file at all'. `expected` is the label both backends must return ("" = show the fallback instead). Run by BOTH src-go/internal/dirs/label_read_test.go and src-tauri/src/dirs.rs's session_label_read_matches_shared_fixture — the same file must produce the same name on the desktop app and on the HTTP backend, and the divergences that matter (bytes vs chars, null vs missing, BOM, trailing data, verbatim whitespace) are exactly the ones a per-language test suite would each excuse on its own terms.

cases.name: plain
cases.why: the shape the client writes

cases.name: chinese-label
cases.input: {"v": 1, "label": "帮我看看 reader.go 为什么 cancel 之后 history 会重复", "auto": true}
cases.expected: 帮我看看 reader.go 为什么 cancel 之后 history 会重复
cases.why: an auto-derived label; non-ASCII must survive both readers

cases.name: hanzi-at-cap
cases.input: {"v": 1, "label": "中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中", "auto": false}
cases.expected: 中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中
cases.why: 120 CHARS = 360 BYTES: kept. A reader that measured bytes would drop what the other keeps (SD-G10)

cases.name: hanzi-over-cap
cases.input: {"v": 1, "label": "中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中", "auto": false}
cases.why: 121 chars / 363 bytes → dropped, not clamped (SD-G9)

cases.name: latin-at-cap
cases.why: boundary, inclusive

cases.name: latin-over-cap
cases.why: one char past the cap is no label

cases.name: future-version-reads
cases.why: v is not checked: an old AlayaFace must not lose a newer one's names

cases.name: unmodelled-field-wrong-type
cases.why: the backend does not model `auto`; its type must not affect the read

cases.name: label-null
cases.why: JSON null is not a name

cases.name: label-missing
cases.why: no label key

cases.name: label-empty
cases.why: empty is absent

cases.name: label-whitespace-only
cases.why: trim decides PRESENCE only

cases.name: padded-label-verbatim
cases.why: trim must NOT rewrite the value shown — normalisation is the writer's job alone

cases.name: label-wrong-type
cases.why: a number is not a name

cases.name: escaped-unicode
cases.why: \u escapes decode the same on both sides

cases.name: bom
cases.why: a BOM breaks JSON parsing on both sides → dropped, not read with the BOM stripped

cases.name: not-json-body
cases.why: corrupt file

cases.name: non-object-body
cases.why: a valid document must be an object

cases.name: trailing-garbage
cases.why: both readers reject trailing data

cases.name: empty-body
cases.why: zero-length file

cases.name: no-file
cases.why: the common case: every session created before G0

write_cases.name: blank-is-accepted-here
write_cases.why: the VALIDATOR accepts blank; the COMMAND then removes the file (no tombstone). Refusing it would make 'clear the name' impossible.

write_cases.name: hanzi-at-cap

document.label: 中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中

write_cases.why: 120 chars = 360 bytes: the cap counts characters (SD-G10)

write_cases.name: hanzi-over-cap

document.label: 中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中中

write_cases.expected: Session label is over the character limit
write_cases.why: one character past it is refused, not truncated

write_cases.name: latin-over-cap
write_cases.expected: Session label is over the character limit

write_cases.name: label-null
write_cases.expected: Session label 'label' must be a string
write_cases.why: JSON null is not a name. Go unmarshals null into a string field WITHOUT an error and into a *string as nil; serde yields Value::Null. Untyped, that made Go accept the document and treat it as a blank label — i.e. DELETE the user's name — while Rust refused it. This case is the reason the pointer check exists.

write_cases.name: label-number
write_cases.expected: Session label 'label' must be a string
write_cases.why: a number is not a name

write_cases.name: label-array
write_cases.expected: Session label 'label' must be a string
write_cases.why: a list is not a name

write_cases.name: non-object-document
write_cases.expected: Session label document must be a JSON object
write_cases.why: the whole store is replace-on-write, so garbage must never land

write_cases.name: null-document
write_cases.expected: Session label document must be a JSON object
write_cases.why: JSON null is not a document

write_cases.name: unmodelled-keys
write_cases.why: fields this build has never heard of must not block a save (SD-G5), whatever their type

write_cases.name: non-ascii-short
write_cases.why: a short non-ASCII name stores fine — the cap is characters, so this is the case a byte-counting writer would wrongly refuse if the limit were lowered

_comment_write: write_cases is the ACCEPT/REFUSE table for storing a label: `document` is the whole payload the client sends, `expected` is "ok" or the exact refusal message both backends must return. The message is compared verbatim because the client shows it to the user; check-backend-parity.sh compares command NAMES and can never see a divergent message. Run by Go handlers.TestLabelWriteTableMatchesSharedFixture and Rust commands::label::tests::write_table_matches_shared_fixture.
